title: Loving Enemies
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Loving enemies means blessing, praying for, and doing good to those who oppose, mistreat, or harm us. This love does not deny evil, but entrusts vengeance to God and reflects the mercy of Christ.
summary: Loving enemies means blessing, praying for, and doing good to those who oppose, mistreat, or harm us. This love does not deny evil, but entrusts vengeance to God and reflects the mercy of Christ.
christFocus: Jesus Christ loved His enemies by praying for those who crucified Him and dying for sinners. His mercy teaches believers to overcome evil with good rather than being ruled by hatred or revenge.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Jesus commands His followers to love their enemies. This is not natural to the flesh. It requires grace, humility, and trust in the Father who is merciful.

Loving enemies does not mean approving evil or abandoning justice. Scripture commands believers to overcome evil with good while leaving vengeance to God.

Enemy love may include prayer, blessing, truthful speech, refusal to retaliate, and practical kindness. It does not require placing oneself in ongoing danger or pretending harm is harmless.

Christ is the pattern. While sinners were enemies, God acted in mercy through Christ. The cross teaches believers that enemy love is costly and God-glorifying.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Hatred can feel powerful, but it often enslaves the heart. Loving enemies frees believers from being ruled by revenge and bitterness.

This doctrine also displays the Gospel. The world expects retaliation, but Christ forms a people who can bless, pray, forgive, and do good while trusting God’s justice.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Bring your enemies before God in prayer. Refuse revenge, ask for grace to bless rather than curse, and seek wisdom about safety and boundaries. Let Christ’s mercy toward you shape your response to those who oppose you.
